## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Vedanāttika* ("The Triad of Feelings") is a constituent section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Nyanatiloka 2007]. In the Abhidhamma classification scheme, the *vedanā-ttika* constitutes the second triad (*tika*) of the matrix (*mātikā*), following the triad of wholesome states (*kusalattika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. The structural treatment of triads in the *Paṭṭhāna* systematically applies conditional relations across standardized investigative chapters, including the chapter on support (*nissaya-vāra*), conjunction (*saṃsaṭṭha-vāra*), association (*sampayutta-vāra*), and questioning (*pañha-vāra*) [Nyanatiloka 2007].

 Machine-assisted analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 196 shared passages across 27 other Pali texts, while finding no cross-language matches meeting the significance threshold [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the text shares its largest blocks of recurring formulas with other Paṭṭhāna treatments of feeling and root triads, most prominently *Kusalattika, Vedanāttika* (Patthana 11.1), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1), and other *Vedanāttika* sections (Patthana 1.3 and Patthana 13.2), as well as the *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 18) [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Kusalattika, Vedanāttika (Patthana 11.1) (§1.1_1–3.1_4 ↔ §9.1_5–14.1_2); Hetuduka, Tika (Patthana 3.1) (§1.1_0–2.1_3 ↔ §140.1_0–142.1); Vedanāttika (Patthana 1.3) (§1.1_1–3.1_2 ↔ §28.0–31.1_1); Vedanāttika (Patthana 13.2) (§1.1_0–4.1 ↔ §1.1_4–4.1); Vedanāttika, Kusalattika (Patthana 11.10) (§1.1_2–3.1_2 ↔ §2.1_5–3.1_6); Kusalattika, Vedanāttika (Patthana 23.1) (§1.1_2–3.1_4 ↔ §13.1_0–18.1_2); Kusalattika, Vedanāttika (Patthana 17.1) (§2.1_1–3.1_2 ↔ §8.1–9.1_3); Kusalattika, Tika (Patthana 5.1) (§2.1_1–3.1_2 ↔ §6.1–9.1)
